newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil rebels attack key north Sri Lanka army base.
newsitem.headline: Tamil rebels attack key north Sri Lanka army base.

text.p: Separatist Tamil Tiger guerrillas launched a pre-dawn attack on a key military base in the northern junction town of Paranthan in the year's first major attack by rebels, military officials said on Thursday.
"The attack is still going on," a government military spokesman in Colombo told Reuters, adding it was too early to give details.

A large number of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas were taking part in the attack, bombarding the camp with artillery and mortars, other military officials in the north and east said.
Casualty figures were not immediately available.

Government forces captured Paranthan, (280 km) 185 miles north of the capital Colombo from the rebels last July. The town is a major road junction at the neck of the government-controlled northern Jaffna peninsula.

The rebels, fighting for independence in the north and east of Sri Lanka, said they killed at least eight soldiers in a separate attack on Tuesday night on the army's northern forward defences in Vavuniya district, 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Colombo.
